turns.question: Which brackets changed material between revisions? From what to what, and why?
turns.answer:
Three brackets have a change notice that records a material change. The records do not give the rev A material for any of them, so I can only state the material it changed to.

| Bracket | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| BR-43365 | Rev A→B, changed to SUS304 [ECO-803381] | Rev A failed salt spray: red rust at the weld bead at 168 h, against a 240 h requirement [TR-119354]. Rev B passed 240 h [TR-127966]. |
| BR-76459 | Rev A→B, changed to SPFH590 [ECO-431230] | The notice gives no reason. Rev A failed static test, with plastic deformation at the bend at 12.6 kN [TR-163650]. Rev B passed static at 20 kN [TR-641818]. |
| BR-32787 | Rev A→B, changed to SPFH590 [ECO-143744] | The notice gives no reason. Rev A failed static test, with plastic deformation at the bend at 2.9 kN against a 5 kN requirement [TR-139121]. Rev C passed at 5 kN [TR-993437]. |

For BR-76459 and BR-32787, the static failure on rev A is the likely motive, but the records don't state it. That is my inference.

The search covered change notices on brackets and returned only these three. Other bracket notices were about coating, thickness, supplier, pockets or tolerance, not material.

turns.question: Do 6061 aluminum brackets fail durability (fatigue) testing more often than SPCC brackets? Give the failure rate for each.
turns.answer:
Yes. In the records, 6061 aluminum brackets fail fatigue testing about twice as often as SPCC brackets. I counted parts, not individual test reports.

| Material | Brackets with a fatigue test | Brackets with at least one fatigue fail | Failure rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| AL6061-T6 | 42 | 14 | 33% |
| SPCC | 50 | 8 | 16% |

- **How I counted:** a bracket counts as failing if it has any fatigue report with a fail result. The counts include reports on every revision, so a failure on an earlier revision that a later revision fixed is still counted.
- **Sample size:** the sample is modest, 42 and 50 parts. The gap is large, but I did not run a significance test.

I can list the failing parts or limit the count to failures on each part's current revision. That would show which failures are still open.

turns.question: 6061 알루미늄 브래킷이 SPCC 브래킷보다 내구(피로) 시험 불합격률이 높아? 각각 불합격률 알려줘.
turns.answer:
네, AL6061-T6 브래킷의 피로 시험 불합격률이 SPCC 브래킷보다 높습니다.

| 소재 | 피로 시험 이력이 있는 브래킷 | 그중 불합격 이력이 있는 브래킷 | 불합격률 |
|---|---|---|---|
| AL6061-T6 | 42개 | 14개 | 약 33.3% |
| SPCC | 50개 | 8개 | 16.0% |

알루미늄 브래킷의 불합격률은 SPCC 브래킷의 약 2배입니다.

- **계산 기준:** 부품 단위로 계산했습니다. 피로 시험 보고서에서 한 번이라도 불합격이 나온 부품을 불합격 부품으로 셌습니다. 모든 리비전의 시험을 포함했습니다.
- **리비전 주의:** 이전 리비전에서 불합격했다가 이후 리비전에서 개선된 부품도 불합격에 포함됩니다. 현재 리비전 기준의 미해결 불합격만 보려면 다시 집계해야 합니다.
- **인용 ID:** 이번 집계는 건수 조회 결과라서 개별 부품 번호와 보고서 ID는 없습니다. 원하시면 불합격 부품 목록을 뽑아 드리겠습니다.

turns.question: Did any part that looks like BR-66254 fail fatigue testing? For the ones that were fixed and are released now, who is the supplier?
turns.answer:
Yes. Two parts with a similar shape failed fatigue testing on rev A, and both were fixed in rev B. Only one of them is released, and its supplier is Supplier 04.

BR-66254 has no test reports of its own. I checked the 20 most similar parts, and these two are the only ones with a fatigue failure.

- **BR-19198 (Bracket 96x83, AL6061-T6):**
  - The rev A fatigue test failed. A crack appeared at the bolt hole after 509k cycles against a 1000k target [TR-381830].
  - ECO-835133 raised the wall thickness from 2.0 to 3.0 mm.
  - Rev B passed fatigue at 1000k cycles [TR-881948] and is Released.
  - The supplier is Supplier 04 (2,240 KRW, 4-week lead time).
- **BR-83689 (Bracket 250x150, AL6061-T6):**
  - The rev A fatigue test failed. It cracked at the bolt hole after 90k cycles against a 200k target [TR-236803].
  - ECO-941845 raised the wall thickness from 2.0 to 3.0 mm.
  - Rev B passed fatigue [TR-225469], but it is still In Work, not Released.
  - ERP lists no supplier for it.

Other similar parts, such as BK-15044 and BK-30632, had rev A failures in dimensional tests, not fatigue.

turns.question: Across our parts, what fixes were used for salt spray failures, and how many parts got each kind of fix? Which was most common?
turns.answer:
Zinc-nickel coating is the most common fix for salt spray failures. The tally below is a lower bound, not a full count. It comes from change notices that my searches returned, and the search results were capped at 20 each. The database has 59 parts with a salt spray fail report, and I could not match every one to its change notice.

| Fix | Parts found | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Zinc-nickel coating added | 15 | BR-26936 [ECO-156903], FS-92678 [ECO-902183], BR-14245 [ECO-823991], BR-74341 [ECO-581500], PL-33713 [ECO-473756] |
| Insulating washer added | 9 | FS-66119 [ECO-715437], BR-91781 [ECO-177690], FS-97797 [ECO-179760], FL-38394 [ECO-606387], FS-52493 [ECO-456665] |
| Material changed to SUS304 | 2 | PL-57750 [ECO-469820], BR-43365 [ECO-803381] |

- **Zinc-nickel coating:** The other parts in this group are BR-62701, PL-88612, BR-27148, FS-30255, BR-49327, BR-27250, PL-39733, FS-54888, PL-96629 and FL-62091. Some of these notices describe the corrosion (cut edges, red rust, weld bead) rather than citing the test report.
- **Insulating washer:** The other parts are BR-79547, FL-87793, FL-85648 and FL-14419. Some notices describe the corrosion without citing the test report, as with the zinc-nickel group.
- **Possible fourth fix:** Two notices change the material to SPFH590, for BR-76459 [ECO-431230] and BR-32787 [ECO-143744]. They don't mention salt spray, so I haven't counted them.

I can try to match each of the 59 failing parts to its change notice, if you want a full count.

turns.question: I'd like to reuse an existing part instead of making BR-66254. Is there anything similar in shape, within 1.5x its size, whose current revision passed fatigue testing?
turns.answer:
Yes. Several parts of similar shape, within 1.5× the size of BR-66254 (60 mm longest side), passed fatigue testing on their current revision. BR-66254 is rev A, In Work, AL6061-T6, 60×40×30 mm. It has no test reports.

The best matches, which are AL6061-T6 like BR-66254:
- **BR-43038** (Bracket 80x80, 90° join): similarity 0.786, size ratio 1.33, Released, rev A. It passed 200k cycles with no fracture [TR-719233].
- **BR-40343** (Bracket 83x76): similarity 0.823, size ratio 1.38, Released, rev A. It passed 200k cycles [TR-428288].

Other options:
- **BR-24601** (Bracket 67x48, SPCC): similarity 0.778, size ratio 1.11, In Work. It passed 1000k cycles [TR-812087].
- **BR-36058** (Bracket 60x16, SPCC): similarity 0.768, size ratio 1.01, Released. It passed 1000k cycles [TR-670788].
- **BR-98978** (Bracket 70x47, SPCC): similarity 0.775, size ratio 1.17, In Work. It passed 500k cycles [TR-883225].
- **PL-10187** (Plate 56x44, AL6061-T6): similarity 0.796, size ratio 0.93, Released. It passed 1000k cycles [TR-596722]. It is only 3.2 mm thick, so it is a flat plate and probably not a good stand-in for an L-bracket.
- **PL-59262** (Plate 50x40, AL6061-T6): similarity 0.774, size ratio 0.83, In Work. Its rev B passed 1000k cycles [TR-727634]. The earlier similarity listing also showed a fail for this part. I didn't read that report, so I can't say which revision it was on.
- **PL-16849** (Plate 41x20, AL6061-T6): similarity 0.778, size ratio 0.69, In Work. It passed 200k cycles [TR-997255]. The similarity listing also showed one fail for this part, which I didn't check.

Shape similarity is only about 0.77–0.82 for all of these, and none is a near-identical shape. BR-43038 and BR-40343 are the closest bracket-type, AL6061-T6 candidates, and both are Released. Compare their geometry and load case with the engine-mount requirement before reusing either. The fatigue cycle counts and load levels also differ between parts.

The block parts, such as BK-23432 and BK-39883, are similar in shape. They did not appear in the list of parts with a passing fatigue report on the current revision, so I left them out.
